correctness.rationale: For a spectrum contained in a line, all exponentials factor through the scalar projection. Completeness therefore forces that projection to be essentially one-to-one on the two segment components. The projected measure has constant density on its support; after scaling the line direction by that density one obtains Lebesgue measure on two disjoint intervals whose lengths are \(c_1T_1\) and \(c_2T_2\) and sum to one. Łaba's exhaustive two-interval theorem then gives exactly the integer-gap lattice case and, only for equal half-lengths, the two-coset case with \(2g+1\in\mathbb N\). The converse follows from the same projection equivalence. The concrete non-lattice example also checks directly.

evidence: Wu treats the same weighted non-coplanar two-segment objects and proves existence plus the projection machinery.
Łaba completely classifies spectra of the projected one-dimensional two-interval support.

Writing \(a=r+g\) produces exactly the assigned integer-gap and \(2g+1=n\) branches.

originality.rationale: The final classification is already covered by direct implication of published results. Wu's primary paper states and proves the exact projection equivalence for line spectra under essential injectivity, and its density-uniformity argument supplies the constant-density reduction. Łaba's Theorem 1.1 exhaustively classifies every spectrum of a two-interval set of total length one as precisely the lattice case or the equal-half-length two-coset case. Substituting the projected lengths and gap into Łaba's notation yields every branch of the assigned theorem mechanically, including the equal-mass restriction. That the weighted skew geometry is not written in the identical notation does not avoid implication coverage.
